name: Thiruvalathoor Temple
description: An ancient Bhagavathy temple known for its woodwork and stone sculpture. Local tradition tells of a surrounding wall left unfinished before daybreak.

name: Chittur Gurumadam
description: A riverside memorial to Thunchath Ezhuthachan, whose Malayalam retellings of the Ramayana and Mahabharata shaped the language’s literary tradition. Manuscripts and objects associated with the poet are part of its heritage.

name: Thenari Sree Rama Temple
description: A place of worship associated with the Ramayana, with a sacred spring beside the temple. Its water is revered in local tradition.

name: Palakkad Fort · Tipu’s Fort
description: Built by Hyder Ali in 1766, this protected fort is one of Palakkad’s best-known landmarks. Its moat, ramparts and grounds offer a view of the town’s history; the Anjaneya shrine stands inside.
endpoint: Fort road approach; walk to entrance

name: Jainimedu Jain Temple
description: A historic granite temple dedicated to Chandraprabha, with images of Jain Tirthankaras. The surrounding neighbourhood is also associated with poet Kumaran Asan and Veenapoovu.

name: Kalpathy Shiva Temple
description: Visit the Vishwanatha Swamy temple and the surrounding agraharam streets. Kalpathy is especially known for its annual chariot festival, Ratholsavam.

name: Kerala Kalamandalam
description: At Cheruthuruthy, this renowned institution preserves Kerala’s traditional performing arts. Arrange a visitor programme in advance if you hope to see teaching or performances.

name: Thiruvegappura Sankaranarayana Temple
description: Also known as the Moonnumoorthy temple, this riverside temple is associated with Shiva, Vishnu and Sankaranarayana. Its traditional koothambalam, or temple theatre, is an important architectural feature.

name: Thrithala
description: Explore a village on the Bharathapuzha known for its temple traditions and the historic Kattil Madom monument nearby. Allow additional travel for individual sites around the village.

name: Guruvayur
description: The Sree Krishna temple is one of Kerala’s important pilgrimage destinations, known for devotional offerings such as Thulabharam. Check temple entry rules and arrangements before travelling.
endpoint: Road approach near Sree Krishna temple

name: Fantasy Park
description: An amusement and water park near Malampuzha, with activities for families. Check the park’s current opening schedule, available rides and entry requirements before visiting.

name: Malampuzha Rock Garden
description: Designed by Nek Chand, the garden turns discarded tiles, bangles, stones and other materials into sculpture. A distinctive art stop in the Malampuzha area.
notice: Kerala Tourism currently reports the main Malampuzha Garden closed, with the dam and ropeway open. Check the latest notice and access to individual attractions before setting out.

name: Malampuzha Dam & Gardens
description: The reservoir, dam and gardens sit below the surrounding hills. The area is also known for Kanayi Kunhiraman’s Yakshi sculpture and the aerial ropeway.
notice: Kerala Tourism currently reports the main Malampuzha Garden closed, with the dam and ropeway open. Check the latest notice and access to individual attractions before setting out.

name: Meenkara Dam
description: A reservoir set in the countryside near the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border. The dam and surrounding landscape make a quieter stop for views of the water and hills.

name: Pothundy Dam
description: An old earthen dam near Nenmara, with reservoir views and a backdrop of the Nelliyampathy hills. It can be a stop on the route towards Nelliyampathy.

name: Meenvallam Waterfalls
description: A forest waterfall on the Thuppanadu river in the Kalladikodan hills. Access involves walking beyond the road approach; check seasonal restrictions and local entry arrangements.
endpoint: Nearest mapped road; final walk extra

name: Mangalam Dam
description: A reservoir bordered by wooded hills and countryside. A place to take in the landscape, with access to visitor areas subject to local conditions.

name: Kanjirapuzha Dam & Garden
description: A broad reservoir framed by hills and forest, with a garden near the dam. Its wooded surroundings and islands form the main attraction.

name: Nelliyampathy
description: A hill area of plantations, wooded slopes and viewpoints reached by a winding mountain road. The estimate is to Nelliyampathy village; individual viewpoints and estates are farther on.

name: Silent Valley National Park
description: A protected rainforest landscape in the Western Ghats. Plan entry through Mukkali with the forest department; organised park transport and entry arrangements are separate from the drive to Mukkali.

name: Parambikulam Tiger Reserve
description: A protected forest landscape in the Anamalai hills, home to diverse wildlife. Contact the reserve about permitted activities, reservations and entry times; wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.

name: Attappadi
description: A wide mountain valley around the upper Bhavani river, beneath the Nilgiri hills. The estimate is to Agali, a practical starting point for the area; onward travel depends on your destination.
